issue.title: Conditional block wrappers

repository.name: pug
repository.description: Pug – robust, elegant, feature rich template engine for Node.js

issue.body:
We're using something like this in Jade (not latest) but Pug doesn't appear to like calls to the same `block` in a single layout. 

Any known workarounds? Thanks.

```
if (!req.headers["x-pjax"])
    doctype html
    html(lang='en-us')
        head
        body
            main
                block content

if (req.headers["x-pjax"])
    main
        block content
```

The above code doesn't display the `content` block in either case.

body: Note that I'm having the same issue when moving from jade->pug - this is existing functionality in jade@1.11.0 which has broken somewhere along the line to pug@2.0.0-alpha8
Are you sure that this works with `jade@1.11.0`? I don't think it was supposed to.

definitely - also described in #2379 suggesting common use case when performing conditional blocks for partial ajax page loads (which is what i am doing).

issue/jade resolution reproducible below taking the /example from pug@2.0.0-alpha8:

### original

$ node examples/extend.js
**_ok_**

### break code

-- extend-layout.pug:

```
html
  head
    h1 My Site - #{title}
    block scripts
      script(src='/jquery.js')
  body
    if(true)
      block content
    else
      block content
    block foot
      #footer
        p some footer content
```

$ node examples/extend.js
**_fails_**

### fix code (by using jade)

$ npm install jade
$ rename "s/.pug/.jade/" ./examples/*.pug

-- extend.js:

```
var pug = require('jade')
  , path = __dirname + '/extend.jade'
  , str = require('fs').readFileSync(path, 'utf8')
  , fn = pug.compile(str, { filename: path, pretty: true });

var tobi = { name: 'tobi', age: 2 };
var loki = { name: 'loki', age: 1 };
var jane = { name: 'jane', age: 5 };

console.log(fn({
    title: 'pets'
  , pets: [tobi, loki, jane]
}));
```

-- extend.jade:

```
extends extend-layout.jade

block scripts
  script(src='/jquery.js')
  script(src='/pets.js')

block content
  h1= title
  each pet in pets
    include pet.jade
```

$ node examples/extend.js
**_ok_**

any effort getting this working in pugjs and preventing dirty workarounds appreciated.
If this worked in jade then I think we should attempt to fix this before the final 2.0.0 release.
@perrin4869 Firt because will need to repeat the parameters for `res.render` and secondly because you don't want to repeat the content of your pages in "mypage.pug" and "mypage_ajax.pug".

Also required for AMP (accelerated mobile pages) and all other scenarios, where you want to dynamically provide the user with another layout of the same content ...

e.g. with a template like this:

```
if isAmp
  include template-amp.pug
else
  include template.pug
```

Lost 4 hours to find this undocumented degradation after `pug` migration. And now had to rollback.
This should be referenced in https://github.com/pugjs/pug/issues/2305. And https://github.com/pugjs/pug/issues/2305 should be referenced in README.md

This is really a party killer for ajax.
@garkin, #2305 is now referenced in the README. And since this is a bug, it won't go into the ticket as those are legitimate changes.

issue.title: Undocumented breaking changes in pug

repository.name: pug
repository.description: Pug – robust, elegant, feature rich template engine for Node.js

issue.body:
Just like you've asked in https://github.com/pugjs/pug/issues/2305 here are two breaking changes I've found updating a mid-large app (~400 jade files) to pug.

https://github.com/antpaw/puggy in this repository you can switch between "pug" and "jade" branches and see how the "pug" branch breaks with exactly the same code.

---

First one is that you can't pass in variables that will be defined later on by pug (e.g. in a loop)

`http://localhost:5000/var`

``` javascript
res.render('var/index', {myVar: { foo: 'bar' }});
```

``` pug
html
  head
    title VAR
  body
    p= myVar.foo
    for myVar in [1, 2, 3]
      p= myVar
```

---

The other one was really hard to find, because the error is very misleading. It's no longer possible to have blocks nested into extends with the same name as a block from a parent.

`http://localhost:5000/block`

It will say that something is wrong with the `block base`, but actually it can't render `block body` because it's defined twice and has some `extend` around it.

``` javascript
Unexpected block base
```

issue.body: Fixes pugjs/pug#2367 and second half of pugjs/pug#2491.

body:
I'm facing the same issue, I try using case and if/else and something that was working before with Jade is no more working with Pug.

``` pug
if (pageType == "masonry")
    block content
else if (pageType == "2cols")
    block content
else
 block content
```

In my index.pug, I have the block content with content inside that is no be printing. Have your an idea when that could be fixed?

@sd65 Couldn’t you use a mixin to achieve this? A mixin with zero parameters is basically the same as a block.

```
// page.pug
mixin content()
  p Hello
```

```
// layout.pug
include page.pug
if (ajax)
  +content()
else
  html 
    head
      ...
    body
      ...
      +content()
```

~~(Also, I’m curious, how did you Markdown two code blocks in a row?)~~
